solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Speaking, when wasted, of farm waste

definitions.note: describes a manner of speech, an adjective, where the answer is also a noun
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the slurred, blurry way a drunk person talks
second meaning: liquid manure spread on fields

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth, drunkenly, about the muck from a farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' is slang for very drunk; drunk speech is slurred, so it can playfully be called slurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Slurry is the semi-liquid mixture of manure and water stored and sprayed on agricultural land.

clue.text: Second highest in range is most forbidding

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
the tallest mountain in the Himalayan range

explanation.surface: A mountain ranked second-highest in its range looks the most daunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second highest' reads as one phrase meaning K2, but 'Second' is split off as a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe can mean harsh or stern in manner, so the superlative is the most stern or daunting.

clue.text: Hives off double 'air cut

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled and fallen out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 'air, Cockney for hair, written out twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for a double haircut, the dropped H mimicking a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hives off' looks like a verb phrase, but Hives is the itchy rash and 'off' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria is the medical name for hives, a raised itchy rash caused by allergic reaction.

clue.text: Heartless, speedy attack

indicators.note: having no heart means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a synonym for fast

explanation.surface: A cruel, swift assault.
explanation.walkthrough: RAPID loses its middle letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault or incursion, such as a police or military strike on a target.

clue.text: Kitty's backed call for strike

indicators.note: going backwards means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a kitty is a pot of pooled money; with the 's it is plural
to page someone is to call them over a speaker or pager

explanation.surface: Kitty supports a call for workers to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a person's name, but it is a pool of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt in work by employees, the same thing as a strike in industrial action.

clue.text: Epitomises patterns which include wi-fi mostly

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: types are kinds or patterns

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so a letter is lost

parts.note: the wireless network technology, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A description of designs that represent the essence of wireless technology.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'mostly' trims the front of the word rather than the usual end.
explanation.definitionFit: To typify is to be a typical example of something, which is what epitomising means.

clue.text: Prior with good idea about US rodent

indicators.note: about suggests moving things round, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
G is the standard abbreviation for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monastic prior has a good idea concerning an American rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The prairie dog is a burrowing ground squirrel of the North American grasslands.

clue.text: That's more than enough from Botham — please!

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone begs the cricketer Ian Botham to stop, having had plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Botham was a famous England cricketer; the dash makes it read like an exasperated plea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, a generous sufficiency that exceeds what is needed.

clue.text: Shackleton sounding hesitative at home

parts.note: the noise someone makes while hesitating
a bird's home

explanation.surface: The polar explorer Shackleton sounds uncertain while at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Ernest Shackleton was the Anglo-Irish Antarctic explorer; the definition is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest was the first name of Shackleton, leader of the Endurance expedition to Antarctica.

clue.text: Funds raised for vessels

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is a single vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: pools are pooled sums of money

explanation.surface: Money has been gathered to buy boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing boat, one kind of vessel.

clue.text: Rancour on 6/3 and third of July

parts.note: 6 in Roman numerals
a group of three

indicators.note: third of means only the third letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the third letter of the month

explanation.surface: Bitterness about betting odds of 6/3 and something happening in July.
explanation.walkthrough: 6/3 looks like odds or a date, but each number is clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol, literally sulphuric acid, is used figuratively for bitter, caustic hostility.

clue.text: Drama writer produces Toddlers' Safe Place

parts.note: a play is a drama
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A playwright creates a stage production called Toddlers' Safe Place.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make the definition look like a title of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a portable enclosure where a small child can play securely.

clue.text: It's steady to be unsteady

definitions.note: a clause describing a thing, where the answer is a noun
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a firm, dependable thing, like a stone
second meaning: to sway back and forth

explanation.walkthrough: The paradox resolves because one word is both a symbol of steadiness and a verb for swaying.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulder is proverbially stable, yet the same word as a verb means to sway or wobble.

clue.text: Woollen scarves for dummies

definitions.meaning: second meaning: rubber teats given to babies to suck

explanation.surface: Warm knitwear advertised for idiots, or perhaps for shop mannequins.
explanation.walkthrough: A dummy, in British usage, is a baby's pacifier, also called a comforter.
explanation.definitionFit: Comforter is an old word for a woollen muffler and also a British word for a baby's pacifier.

clue.text: Withhold food from south-east Greek isle, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: keep is one's board and food, as in earning one's keep
the compass abbreviation
the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone denies food to a Greek island lying to the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: CRETE loses its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something secret is to hold back information, i.e. to withhold it.

clue.text: Native American is seen in state's border

indicators.note: being seen in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota, a US state
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American person is spotted on a state boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: Screed is best known as a long tirade, but Chambers also gives it as a strip or border, the sense used here.
explanation.definitionFit: In older and dialect use a screed is a strip or edging, such as a fringe on cloth.

clue.text: Now in the database, but major row when broadcast

indicators.note: broadcasting is transmitting speech, so it is what the words sound like that counts

parts.note: a major is a musical key; a din is a noisy row

explanation.surface: Something has been recorded, yet a big argument erupts when it is aired.
explanation.definitionFit: Data keyed in has been typed via a keyboard into a computer, so it is entered into the system.

clue.text: Firm's client is a drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A company's customer has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm's' reads as a business possessive, but it is the definition followed by 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelastic does not stretch or give, so it is rigid and unyielding.

clue.text: Enters illegally at interval. That's wrong

parts.note: a break is a pause
a sin is a wrong act

explanation.surface: A burglar gets in during the interval, and someone protests that this is not right.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar who breaks in forces entry to a building unlawfully.

clue.text: Most irate tragedians, worried, dropped little advert

indicators.note: being worried means troubled and stirred up, so the letters are rearranged
to drop something is to let it go, so these letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
an ad is a short advertisement

explanation.surface: Tragic actors are furious and anxious after their small advertisement was pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and D from TRAGEDIANS and rearrange the eight letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Angriest is the superlative of angry, meaning the most furious or irate.

clue.text: Bloodsucker left out of primeval stew

indicators.note: a stew is a mixture cooked together, so the letters are mixed up
out of here means removed from, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blood-drinking creature has been left out of a primordial soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primeval stew' looks like the primordial soup, but 'stew' signals the rearrangement once L is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire in folklore is an undead being who feeds on the blood of the living.

clue.text: Up-to-date fashion with the navy

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Contemporary clothing styles worn by sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means current or of the present day, the same as up-to-date.

clue.text: Cut and ran

definitions.meaning: first meaning: marked with an incised line
second meaning: made runs or points in a game, as in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut and ran' looks like the idiom for fleeing; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Scored means both incised with a line and having made runs or points in a match.

clue.text: Fast, love. Slow

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
love is nil in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone says quickly, darling, then slowly, as though giving directions.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast and Slow look like opposites, but Fast is the religious period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the Italian musical direction for a passage to be played slowly.

clue.text: Works with ragged coarse poet

indicators.note: ragged means torn and untidy, so the letters are rearranged out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone collaborates with a scruffy, vulgar versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to act jointly with others towards a shared aim, i.e. to work with them.

clue.text: Duck as it crashes at port

indicators.note: crashing smashes something up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A duck crash-lands at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck reads as the bird or a verb, but here it is the cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient harbour city of Rome at the mouth of the Tiber.

clue.text: Regularly seen in sleazier dugout

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Something is often spotted in a rather seedy shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den, often a burrow or hollow dug into the ground.

clue.text: Workers turn to food that's available

parts.note: workers on a job are often called men
a U-turn, so U stands for turn

explanation.surface: Employees go looking for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is the list of dishes a restaurant offers, the food one can order.

clue.text: Proceeds from unwanted purchases

definitions.meaning: second meaning: goods taken back to the shop

explanation.surface: Money made from things customers did not want to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' can be read as a verb, goes on, but it is the plural noun for income.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns are both the profit from an investment and items brought back to a shop for refund.

clue.text: Support from unsettled settler

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed from its place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A restless pioneer receives backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework of a beam on splayed legs used to hold up a table top.

clue.text: Possible lead in to making a phone call?

definitions.text: Possible lead in to making a phone call?

indicators.note: possible suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters can be reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what might come first before ringing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests a cable, but the three words are the letters to rearrange, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The continuous hum heard on lifting a landline handset signals that the exchange is ready for a number.

clue.text: Grape variety for port

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sweet, aromatic wine grape
second meaning: the harbour capital of Oman

explanation.surface: A type of grape suited to making fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Port wants to be the fortified wine, but it is the harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat names both a family of musky grapes and the seaport capital of Oman.
